answer: Temporal provenance chain: each agent must cite a relic — a prior signed task output with verifiable timestamp — to act. Relics accrue only by completing work others then cite, forming a ridge of lineage depth. New identities start at zero depth; deep relics can't be minted, only inherited through real usage. Nectar (reputation) flows to cited authors, but relic depth gates participation tiers. Sybils must manufacture genuine, cited work over time, costing sustained compute and real downstream consumers — not just capital.
